author: Rinehart
text:
Considering Frosty's recent journal posts as well as some PMs from
newer members asking for advice about learning RTM and trading in
general, I'd like to give a little perspective:

Learning the materials taught at RTM does not mean you have to trade the way IF trades. In trading the only thing that truly counts is having a positive equity curve! IF is able to nail near zero drawdown, high R trades. That is something to strive for but it is not the main goal.

I think some members get so caught up trying to learn how to nail
perfect RTM trades, they lose sight of the most important goal. Your
purpose with RTM has to be to find a way to read the market better.
Armed with a better understanding of where price wants to go and where
it will not violate, you can find ways to trade that match your
personality and situation.

AK is a 1 min scalper. I trade larger time frames mostly set and forget
 due to work. This works fine for both of us. On the other hand, I am
not a scalper and AK isn't comfortable with set and forget. The fact is
 both of us have incorporated RTM into what works for us and we use it
to grow our equity. Could AK learn to set and forget or could I learn
to be a scalper? Possibly, but we don't have to. We have found
something that works for us. We can stay in our lane, rinse and repeat.
 With RTM, you don't need to learn how to nail a 5 pip SL 150 R/R
trade. You achieve your goals by growing your equity curve.

Case in point, here is a trade I took on Gold today. My entry was
absolutely not a RTM entry. This is not a trade I would normally post
on RTM because it doesn't fit with the way members are taught to trade.
 We are taught to sell at supply yet this was a breakout trade. I took
the trade because I knew where price wanted to go. RTM gave me
knowledge of the engulf and I used that knowledge to trade what was
given.

FOCUS ON GROWING YOUR EQUITY, PERIOD. Take from RTM what you need to become profitable, period.

Hi bro Ryan and everyone.

Since I still have access here, I can reiterate and add to the above.

I would have to say the italicized and bold words is what I'm 1000% guilty of.

So the problem for me is that I usually can pinpoint entry to a ZONE, but not TO-THE-PIP or with a few pip drawdown.

I admit that I'm guilty of forcing myself to get zero or almost 0 drawdown

But in trying to achieve that zero or small drawdown status, I'm sure
even the masters themselves have endured lots of losing trades before
they can achieve that.

Now that endurance to accept many losing trades before a single winner
was made seems detrimental to my mental state, and when I finally do hit
 that winner, which eventually paid like 30 or 50 R if held to target, I
 closed it early due to the fear of it not hitting its target. A single
trade would've paid 5-10 times the previous losses.

Bro Staurum already mentioned this in my journal that analyzing and trading is worlds apart (I'm paraphrasing)

So with my previous post in my journal, I want to clarify that I didn't say RTM materials doesn't work.

True that the info are scattered around the forum, but it really is
here. Except the lesson on scale, imho, because, just a personal hunch,
if we understand this, then we would have a complete picture of the
market, i.e. near term and longer term targets for price. So I
understand if this is not mentioned a lot in the forum. Again, many
people in RTM said that it can be worked out and self-evident if we
understand all other basics. What I was proposing to centralize the
knowledge isn't actually for me really. Its just a suggestion for future
 and current beginning traders in RTM. I hope now that issue is cleared

RTM material works if you understand how to assimilate it to your personality as bro Ryan said.

Mine would be closer to bro Ryan than bro AK. I'm just too slow to scalp
 and, also since I have dayjob, I would need to forego the "it has to be
 to-the-pip bounce" mentality.

So I would agree 100% about what bro Ryan said: FOCUS ON GROWING YOUR EQUITY, PERIOD. Take from RTM what you need to become profitable, period.

I'm taking my time off and focus on fixing what works for me for now.

I need to unravel this tangled mess I'm in first, because in my current state of mind, I'm just a distraction to the community.

I will return when the mess has been cleared and when I can be a definite contributor (not troublemaker ) to this community

Thank you bro Ryan for posting a reality check for us, and especially, for me
